text:
Brendan Gallagher spent 14 seasons in Montreal and left as the Canadiens' leader in games, goals and points since his debut, according to the club. In June they traded him to Vancouver for future considerations and kept half his salary, a move the Canucks framed around his ties to the Lower Mainland, where he became the Vancouver Giants' all-time leading scorer.

Seventeen games in, he is still looking for his first goal as a Canuck. He has 3.0 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and nothing to show for it, and his team has scored 4.0 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. That reads more like bad luck than a player who has stopped getting to the net: he is averaging 10.7 minutes a night and still finding looks.

The harder part is the context. Vancouver has not won in his last ten games (one of those losses came in overtime), and his 5v5 shot share sits at 43.5%. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season (86th percentile among forwards), so watch whether the chances keep coming. If they do, the goals usually follow.
headline: Gallagher's chances are there. The goals aren't, yet
